title.narrative: Supporting the implementation of the New Urban Agenda. Spain – Latin America and the Caribbean region

description.narrative:
Since 2009, the Ministry of Housing and Urban Agenda (MIVAU) has provided an annual contribution of €110,000 to UN-Habitat. This ongoing support aims to foster collaboration between Spain and Latin America and the Caribbean (LAC) on urban development issues and advance the implementation of the New Urban Agenda (NUA) in Spain. This project proposal seeks to sustain and consolidate this long-standing partnership, ensuring continuity in the objectives and outcomes of successive contributions. The specific activities to be implemented are jointly determined each year, reflecting a dynamic and evolving approach.
For the 2024-2025 contribution (granted at the end of 2024 and implemented in 2025), the project builds upon the successful completion of the previous phase in November 2024. During the 2024 phase, a curated selection of practical case studies was developed, showcasing the implementation of the NUA in the LAC region. These cases, compiled in the document Catalogo Buenas Practicas REV 2dic.pdf, were inspired by a similar catalogue of good urban practices created in Spain. The 2025 activities will focus on disseminating this knowledge and facilitating the exchange of experiences between Spain and the LAC region, furthering mutual learning in urban agenda implementation.
In addition to knowledge dissemination, this phase will continue to emphasize advocacy and communication efforts to strengthen the application of the NUA in Spain. Looking ahead, the proposed framework for subsequent years (2025-2026 and 2026-2027) will follow a similar logic. One year will focus on generating new knowledge products (2025-2026), while the following year will be dedicated to disseminating this knowledge and fostering exchange (2026-2027). This cycle ensures a sustained and impactful collaboration that advances urban development objectives across regions.
Context and Background
By 2030, we will not meet most SDG 11 targets without major shifts in urban policy and investments in local government. The consequences of not achieving SDG 11 in particular are immense, directly impacting billions of people’s daily lives.
According to the Report “Rescuing SDG 11 for a Resilient Urban Planet by 2030”, published by UN-Habitat in 2023, achieving SDG 11 in seven years before 2030 requires urgent and large-scale policy interventions and investments in sustainable. The progress observed in some areas points to a clear opportunity to turn the tide and rescue SDG 11 globally. Yet governments will need to prioritize the most effective interventions given the obvious limits to the scale and scope of their future actions amidst competing demands and resource constraints. Striking this balance is perhaps one of the central difficulties at hand for decision makers facing limited resources yet vast demands and needs arising from global urbanization, one of the mega-trends of the 21st century.
Some progress has been made toward SDG 11 targets related to transport and national urban policies, yet vast gaps remain in the other areas such as slum proliferation, inadequate public space and insufficient waste management.
Empowered cities and local governments can drive transformative shifts in crisis recovery and sustainable development. Providing them with tools, resources, and scientific data is crucial for mobilizing action at scale. By involving local governments in the design and implementation of responses such as addressing migration and displacement challenges, cities can contribute to positive growth and effective solutions.
In 2019, the Ministry of Transports, Mobility and Urban Agenda (currently, MIVAU) approved the Spanish Urban Agenda (AUE, in Spanish), as a National Urban Policy to transfer the global objectives and agreements to the Spanish territorial context and to encourage their implementation by the other Public Administrations, particularly by the Local Administration.
One of the commitments included in the Action Plan of the aforementioned AUE has been the creation of networks and the participation of the Ministry in national and international networks and exchange of knowledge and experiences that, with real content, allows it to continue advancing in the implementation of the AUE, which favors its implementation and generates new work mechanics that, in addition, within the framework of this Agreement, help to strengthen the relationship between Spain and the Latin American and Caribbean Region with the support and collaboration of the UN-Habitat.
In this line of work, collaboration is reflected in the participation and coordination of activities linked to the Urban Forum of Spain, which celebrated its second edition in October 2023 and the participation of the Ministry in the Regional Housing and Habitat Forum which is held every two years and which, in 2023, took place in Bogotá (Colombia), with great success in attendance and participation.
